title: The beach
description: Name the things on a beach, and say where they are.
grammar: gender and articles, and prepositions of place
grammarNote: Words for places and things at the sea follow the same article rules as everything else.

explanation.summary: The beach has its own small set of nouns, and most of them are feminine. The plural is worth noticing, because one of them loses its ending.

sections.heading: The nouns
sections.body: La orilla, la arena, la ola, la concha, la sombrilla, la espuma, la roca and el castillo de arena are feminine. El bañador and el cubo are masculine. El castillo de arena is a whole phrase, and it takes el like other masculine nouns.

sections.heading: At the edge of the sea
sections.body: La orilla is where the water meets the sand. You say a thing is at the edge with en la orilla, and inside the water with en el agua. One word is special: la concha becomes las conchas in the plural, but el cubo becomes los cubos.

examples.es: la sombrilla está en la arena
examples.en: the parasol is on the sand

examples.es: los niños están en el agua
examples.en: the children are in the water

items.note: Masculine: el bañador. The accent marks the stress.
Masculine: el cubo. It is also a word for a cube.
Masculine: el castillo de arena. A phrase with el in front of it.

drills.meaning: the sandcastle is on the sand
drills.note: Castillo is masculine, so el castillo de arena.
